title: A Ember for the Sigil
premise: Wren Underhill carves bone charms in Hollowmere, a valley warded so thoroughly that magic cannot enter—and neither can the truth of why he hears the dead. When he finds tonight's date inscribed in a century-old prophecy book, he learns the valley's wards were built on a broken covenant between the living and the dead, and that his gift marks him as the heir meant to reforge it. Hunted by the Ashen Court, which feeds on severed souls, Wren flees the only home he's known with a ragged band of outcasts who become the family he never had. In the climax at the Sigil's shattered heart, Wren must choose between restoring his own stolen identity or sacrificing it to bind the realms together—and he discovers that belonging was never something to find, but something to build.
about_author: Sebastian Montrose is the pen name of a former mortuary archivist who spent a decade cataloguing epitaphs before turning to fantasy. They write stories about quiet people dragged into loud destinies, and they still can't pass a graveyard without taking notes.

chapters.title: The Date That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. While carving a memorial charm for a grieving widow, Wren hears the dead whisper a warning: 'the book has your name.' He finds a prophecy volume in the chapel archive with tonight's date inked a century ago—beside a sketch of his own face. Emotional beat: dread cracking open a carefully invisible life.

chapters.title: What the Valley Forgets
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Digging into Hollowmere's founding records, Wren learns the valley's magic-dead wards weren't protection but a prison—one that severs souls from the realm beyond. The dead he hears are trapped echoes. His grandmother's deathbed riddles finally make sense. Emotional beat: the vertigo of learning your whole life was a cage.

chapters.title: Ash at the Door
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. An emissary of the Ashen Court arrives wearing a neighbor's face, offering Wren 'peace' if he surrenders his gift. Wren refuses; that night the wards begin to fail and the first trapped soul crosses over—a child who calls him 'keeper.' Emotional beat: fear hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Outcasts on the Ridgeline
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Wren and Sable, a disgraced sigil-smith exiled from the outer realm. Sable's party—Tamsin, a hedge-witch; Brannoc, a soul-ferryman gone mute—crosses the failing wards hunting the prophecy's heir. Instead of enemies, Wren bargains for passage out. Emotional beat: wary alliance, the first spark of found family.

chapters.title: The Road of Small Kindnesses
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The company travels the corpse-road toward the Sigil, and Wren quietly mends things no one asked him to: Tamsin's cracked focus-stone, Brannoc's silence via a carved whistle that lets him 'speak' through birdsong. Sable realizes the prophecy's heir is ordinary in every way but one. Emotional beat: tenderness as resistance.

chapters.title: The Court of Hungry Names
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Captured by the Ashen Court, Wren is shown a mirror-vault where his true name is kept—the identity stripped from him as an infant to power the valley's wards. The Court offers it back in exchange for abandoning the covenant. He escapes with Tamsin's help but leaves knowing what he lost. Emotional beat: longing versus duty.

chapters.title: Bone Remembers
chapters.summary: Brannoc's POV (through Wren's translations). At the ferryman's ruined waystation, Brannoc regains fragments of speech and reveals he ferried Wren's mother across the veil—she gave up her name willingly to hide her son. Grief and gratitude braid together around the campfire. Emotional beat: inheritance redefined as love, not blood.

chapters.title: The Breaking of the Sigil
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The company reaches the Sigil's shattered heart and finds the covenant's anchor stone defaced—by Sable's own former guild, a century ago. Sable confesses their exile was penance for the guild's crime. Trust fractures just as the Ashen Court descends. Emotional beat: betrayal, confession, and the choice to stay anyway.

chapters.title: A Name Given Freely
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Climax. To reforge the covenant, a living soul must surrender its name into the anchor stone. Wren offers not his stolen birth-name but the one he built himself—Wren Underhill, carver, keeper, friend. The dead rise to witness; the Court unravels starved of severed souls. Emotional beat: selfhood as an act of giving, not reclaiming.

chapters.title: Hollowmere, Unhidden
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Months later, the wards are windows, not walls: the dead visit, magic hums gently, and Hollowmere becomes a haven for the displaced. Wren teaches bone-carving to ghost-touched children while Sable, Tamsin, and Brannoc build homes nearby. The prophecy book now ends mid-sentence—unwritten. Emotional beat: belonging, chosen and shared.
